messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: HIGH — Private VPC customers are seeing increased 401/502 errors and latency for cross-region requests (eu-west1 -> us-central1). Alerting threshold breached (5xx+401 > 8% over 5m).

samir: I’m on it. Paging oncall, handoff in 3m if not resolved. I’ll start triage on the ILB + auth proxy path.

pagerduty-bot: Paging samir (on-call, eng-sre).

mira: I’m awake — joining. seeing a spike in our customer error dashboard for private-vpc routes crossing regions. Most errors are 401s from auth-proxy and 502s from the ILB backend.

joel: Confirmed in logs: large number of requests from eu-west1 to us-central1 have header X-CUSTOMER-ID stripped or normalized. Auth proxy rejects (no client header) -> 401. Some requests end up being retried causing 502 from backend pool exhaustion.

eve: Impact scope: ~7 private VPC customers on cross-region routing, intermittent but sustained for ~12 minutes. Public hosted API unaffected.

samir: Possible causes: GCP started enforcing a header-normalization change on internal ILB egress, or an upstream NAT/egress change at GCP messing with preserved headers. Opening GCP support ticket and collecting packet traces.

samir: Quick mitigation options: 1) temporarily force cross-region traffic to use region-local ingress (prefer eu-west1) via routing policy. 2) fallback auth-proxy to token introspection if header missing. 3) ask GCP to roll back header rewriting.

mira: Start with 2) and 1) in parallel. Joel, can you flip auth-proxy config to accept token introspect? I’ll prepare a routing policy change to prefer eu-west1.

joel: On it. Pushing a hotfix to auth-proxy to accept Authorization header introspect when X-CUSTOMER-ID missing. Patch and deploy:

```
# auth-proxy: enable token introspection fallback
kubectl -n infra set env deploy/auth-proxy TOKEN_INTROSPECT_FALLBACK=true
kubectl -n infra rollout restart deploy/auth-proxy
```

joel: Rolling. Watching logs.

support-bot: Noted — updating incident page & customer messages. Draft to customers affected: "We’re investigating increased 401/502 errors for cross-region Private VPC traffic; we’ve applied a temporary mitigation and will follow up with root cause."

samir: Routing change now: adding policy to prefer eu-west1 for private-vpc customer routes (traffic steering). Command:

```
gcloud compute network-endpoint-groups update NEG-PRIVATE-VPC-eu --region=eu-west1 --connection-drain-timeout=30
# and update our routing weights to prefer eu-west1
```

mira: I applied the routing weight tweak; weight eu-west1 -> 90, us-central1 -> 10 for affected customer pools. Monitoring.

joel: Auth-proxy rollout succeeded. Saw immediate drop in 401s from auth-proxy logs where token introspect covered missing header cases. Error rate down to ~3% now.

eve: Customer-observed error rate dropping. Opening message to affected tenants now.

support-bot: Sent messages to tenants with Incident ID INC-1964028300. Included workaround and ETA for more info.

gcp-liaison: GCP support replied — they observed an experimental header normalization rule hitting ILBs in eu-west1 for some internal egress paths. They’re rolling a rollback in next 15-30m; asked for packet captures and forwarding rules we modified. Ticket: https://console.cloud.google.com/support/cases/CH-12345 (redacted)

samir: Good. Keep routing pref to eu-west1 until GCP confirms rollback. Also enable additional rate limits to avoid backend exhaustion if retries spike.

joel: Adding temporary circuit-breaker to backend pool:

```
# enable circuit breaker on envoy pool
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" https://internal-admin/api/v1/circuit-breakers \
  -d '{"pool":"private-vpc-cross-region","max_pending_requests":200}'
```

mira: Circuit breaker in place. Backend pending request stats back to normal.

samir: On-call Handoff: I’ll remain until rollback is confirmed. If rollback takes >45m, Mira take next shift. Handing active on-call to Mira at +40m if unresolved.

pagerduty-bot: Handoff scheduled — samir -> mira at 1964028570.

joel: GCP rollback started. They also noted that an internal egress proxy A/B test was leaking header rewrite rules to some ILB paths. They’ll run verification.

eve: Observability vendor (edge-trace) showed a drop in cross-region trace headers at the same time — filing an incident with them too (they confirm a deployment at ~1964028180 that may have affected header propagation). Created ticket ET-9876.

samir: Because multiple providers changed around same window, we’ll include both GCP and edge-trace in root cause scope. For now, mitigations: auth-proxy fallback, routing weight change, circuit-breaker. These are holding.

support-bot: Status page updated to "partial service disruption affecting some Private VPC cross-region requests — mitigations applied".

mira: I’m taking over active pager. Samir, leaving notes in the runbook: steps performed, commands, GCP & edge-trace tickets, customer list.

samir: Thanks. Leaving detailed action items in the incident doc. Good job team.

gcp-liaison: GCP confirms rollback complete — header normalization reverted at 1964028650. They advise keeping routing weights for 10m to validate.

joel: Observability shows stable headers restored and 401/502 back to baseline. Will keep token introspect fallback for now but schedule safe rollback in staging tomorrow.

eve: Customer confirmations trickling in — support closed active P1 chats as mitigated. No data loss reported.

support-bot: Updated customers with post-mitigations note and ETA for RCA (72h).

mira: Closing the active page once we validate 30m of stable metrics. I’ll notify when we move to postmortem.

samir: Moving to handoff complete. Great coordination. Postmortem owners: mira (lead), joel (auth), eve (customer comms). Assigning follow-ups in tracker.

incident-bot: Incident marked: mitigated -> monitoring. Severity: P1 -> P2. Resource links: internal incident doc: https://redwood/internal/incidents/1964028300 (redacted).
